# dsh-session-metrics

Session **cost and billing** metrics for the DSH Web GUI — what this conversation cost, what the
cac

he saved, and whether the current hour is peak or off-peak. Built as a companion to the shipped
stat
s pills, never a duplicate of them.
## Why

The shipped stats pills report tokens and context, and stop short of money. That leaves three
questi
ons unanswered, and the obvious answer to each is a lie:

**A model with no rate card is not free.** An unpriceable provider reads `unpriced` and shows its
to

kens; a genuinely free model ships a card of zeros and reads a real `$0.00`. The two must not
render
alike — `unpriced` means *no card*, and an unpriced pair is never rendered as a number.
**A newly integrated provider arrives silently.** DSH reports usage per provider and model; rates ar

e
configuration. Integrate a provider before its rates are entered — the case that happened with
Ope

nRouter — and every figure for it is missing with nothing on the page saying why. The session
detail
names the pair it observed with no card, and the tokens it used.
**Peak pricing is invisible until it is a surprise.** DeepSeek bills peak and off-peak at different

rates, in the provider's own timezone. Whether *right now* is peak is not something a user should
ha

provider's own timezone. Whether *right now* is peak is not something a user should
have to derive.
## Agent Skills
Installing the plugin registers the **`session-metrics`** skill, so an agent can explain the figures
and reconfigure the rates without reading the source. Ask it what a session cost, whether a model i

s
priced, or how to add a rate card for a provider it has seen.

ally loads. It is generated; never hand-edit it.

> **Restart, don't reload.** The host half loads once per app process, so a host-side change needs a

## How it Works
Costs are derived from the Host's own `tokenUsage` projection — the same source the stats pills read
— so this plugin adds interpretation, not a second ledger. Cache savings compare each cache-hit tok

en
against the rate that would have been paid on a miss, per the card in effect. Peak and off-peak
w
indows resolve in the provider's own timezone, holidays included, and the countdown is computed once
a minute while the detail view is open rather than on every render.
Two surfaces, one projection:

- **the strip**, below the composer: cost, cache savings, the peak state with your local time, the
p

rovider when it is not your configured primary, and budget progress;
- **the detail**, on click: the

cost breakdown (cache-hit / miss / write / output), cache savings and
blended rate, the rate window

with a countdown, cost per step, cost per model when a session
switched models, and the projections
each figure came from.
The plugin deliberately does **not** render session token totals, cache-hit rate, context percentage

,
turns, steps or tok/s — the shipped pills own those. `docs/data-sources.md`
records which projecti

on feeds which figure, which is what keeps the two from drifting back into
duplication.
### Requirements

- **DSH** with the Web GUI, and a profile you can edit (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/`).
- **Node.js 2

2+** and **pnpm** to build from source. The built artifact needs nothing extra at
runtime.
## What it looks like

The strip as it docks under the composer, at the width the app actually gives it: DSH's own
`compute

Columns()` resolves a 1440×900 window to a 280px sidebar and a **1160px** centre column, and
that is
the canvas below. Every colour is one of the app's theme tokens.
| light | dark |
The detail popover behind the trigger — cost breakdown, saving breakdown, per-model rows, and the pe

ak
window with its countdown.
| light | dark |

Both come from `scripts/capture-panel.mts`, which renders the **real** bundle through
`test/harness.

ts` — the same path the DOM tests take — injects the **real** stylesheet the bundle
itself ships, an

d resolves the `--dsw-*` tokens out of the installed `app.asar`. Nothing is mocked and
no colour is
hand-picked. Run it with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

One honest gap: the popover is captured **standalone**, centred by a layout wrapper, rather than
anc
hored under the strip. Its `left`/`bottom` come from a live `getBoundingClientRect()` of the docked

trigger, and the headless renderer has no layout engine to produce one — so its content, width and
s
tyles are real, and only the frame around it is not.
